question: In the roaches pest-control study (Gelman and Hill; Regression and Other Stories), how much lower is the expected number of roaches caught per trap-day in treated apartments than in control apartments, adjusting for the pre-treatment roach level and senior-building status?

estimand.description: Log rate ratio of expected roaches per unit exposure for treatment versus control, holding pre-treatment level and senior status fixed; beta[1] under the coding X = [roach1/100, treatment, senior]

decisions.reason: Start with the textbook Poisson regression with a log link, log(exposure2) as an offset, a Normal(0, 2.5) prior on the intercept, and independent Normal(0, 2.5) priors on the three slopes. Conditional variance is forced to equal the mean. Retain a posterior predictive check on the count distribution before revising.

interpretation: The Poisson baseline is a deliberate starting point. Read the retained posterior check for whether the predicted count distribution reproduces the observed spread and the number of zero counts; it is not an automatic verdict.
unresolved_questions: Does the Poisson variance assumption reproduce the observed dispersion and the 94 zero counts out of 262?
Is the treatment effect sensitive to how the pre-treatment roach level enters the model?
Is a single shared treatment effect adequate across senior and non-senior buildings?
